newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures seen opening steady.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures seen opening steady.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open unchanged Thursday following a move to the upside Wednesday on news of a reduction in power at the Palo Verde nuclear power unit.
August Palo Verde (PV) was pegged at $34.70 per megawatt hour (MWh) in over the counter discussion Thursday, unchanged from Wednesday's NYMEX August PV close.

August PV was said to have dipped early Thursday in over-the-counter talk on news the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) approved late Wednesday a final summertime capacity for the Pacific Intertie of 6,900 megawatts (MW). The new rating will replace an interim summer cap of 6,300 MW which has been in place since July 1.
August PV later rebounded, sources said. "Basically we are looking unchanged," said one electricity futures trader.
August California Oregon Border (COB) was seen opening steady from Wednesday's close at $21.01 per MWh.
"We thought with the intertie news that COB would be higher and PV lower, but it's not looking that way now," the futures trader said.

Futures prices climbed Wednesday on news the 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde nuclear power complex in Arizona will begin Sunday to slowly ramp down to between 60 and 80 percent power by September 6, when it scheduled to shut for refueling, the operator Arizona Public Service Co said.

Also in generation news, the 1,070 MW SONGS unit 2 at the in southern California was at 98 percent power early Thursday, while the neighboring 1,080 MW unit 3 was at 86 percent and was increasing to full power.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be coolest over the central and eastern sections over the next week, averaging three to five degrees Fahrenheit below normal, with readings one to two degrees below normal in the west.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to average three to five degrees below normal over most of the region through into early next week, with temperatures near normal in the extreme east, south and west sections.
